record.paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: For β-skeletons with parameter β in the interval [1, 2], determine whether the known upper bound (n−1)^γ on the spanning ratio, where γ = 1 − log2(√(2/β)), is tight for all β in that range.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 11. For the range β ∈ [1, 2], is the upper bound on the spanning ratio of (n−1)^γ, where γ = 1 − log2(√(2/β)), tight? It is tight for the GG, where β = 1 and RNG, where β = 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let P be a finite set of n points in the plane in general position. For a real parameter β ≥ 1, the β-skeleton of P is the undirected graph on vertex set P in which two distinct points p, q ∈ P are joined by an edge if and only if the open "lune" region

  L_β(p,q) = D_1 ∩ D_2,

contains no point of P \ {p,q}, where D_1 and D_2 are the two open disks of radius (β/2)·|pq| whose boundaries pass through p and q and whose centers lie on the line through p and q at distance (β/2 - 1/2)·|pq| on opposite sides of the midpoint of pq (so β = 1 yields the Gabriel graph GG and β = 2 yields the relaxed/relative neighborhood graph RNG, in the "lune-based" definition).

The spanning ratio of a connected geometric graph G on P is

  sr(G) = max_{p,q ∈ P, p ≠ q}  d_G(p,q) / |pq|,

where d_G is shortest-path distance in G with Euclidean edge weights. For β ∈ [1,2], it is known that every β-skeleton on n points satisfies

  sr ≤ (n − 1)^γ,   where γ = 1 − log₂(√(2/β)).

The bound is known to be tight at the endpoints β = 1 (Gabriel graph) and β = 2 (relative neighborhood graph).

Problem. Decide whether the upper bound sr ≤ (n−1)^γ is tight for every β ∈ [1,2]; that is, for each β ∈ [1,2], does there exist, for arbitrarily large n, an n-point set P in the plane whose β-skeleton has spanning ratio Θ((n−1)^γ)?
artifact.status_search_result: Search results indicate that the upper bound (n−1)^γ on the spanning ratio of β-skeletons for β ∈ [1,2], established by Bose, Devroye, Evans, and Kirkpatrick (SIAM J. Discrete Math., 2006, building on a 2002 conference version), is known to be tight only at the endpoints β = 1 (Gabriel graph) and β = 2 (relative neighborhood graph). No source found establishes tightness for intermediate β, and the question of closing the gap appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On the Spanning Ratio of Gabriel Graphs and beta-Skeletons
status_evidence.snippet: Bounds on the exponent of n in upper and lower bounds for the spanning ratio of β-skeletons; tightness shown at β=1 and β=2.
status_evidence.claim: Tightness is established at the endpoints β=1 and β=2 but the intermediate range remains a gap.

status_evidence.title: On the Spanning Ratio of Gabriel Graphs and β-Skeletons (preprint)
status_evidence.snippet: Upper bound (n−1)^γ with γ = 1 − log2(√(2/β)) for β ∈ [1,2].
status_evidence.claim: Upper bound formula matches the one in the problem; matching lower bound is only known at the endpoints.

status_evidence.title: Beta skeleton — Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses spanning properties of β-skeletons including Gabriel graph and RNG cases.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference confirming the definitions and known endpoint cases.
